Our secret to leading the way in hospitality? We put our people first!

At Shake Shack, our mission is to Stand For Something Good in all that we do. From our teams to our neighborhoods, we're committed to always doing the right thing. As one of the fastest-growing hospitality brands, we're all about crafting unforgettable experiences for our guests. We offer endless learning opportunities and the chance to make a lasting impact on our business, restaurants, and communities. As a member of the #ShackFam, you’ll have access to hands-on mentorship, training, and growth potential, all in a fun and inclusive environment.

Join us and Be a Part of Something Good.

Oversees the ongoing maintenance, repairs, and facilities needs of existing Shack locations to ensure facilities and equipment are properly maintained. Leads the planning and execution of facility upgrades, remodels, and refresh projects. Establishes and monitors preventative maintenance programs and vendor performance to support consistent and timely maintenance across the restaurant portfolio. Partners with Operations teams to provide training and guidance on the ongoing maintenance of their Shacks. Leads, develops, and mentors Facilities Managers to ensure effective execution of facilities initiatives.


Job Responsibilities and Duties

• Oversee the ongoing facilities, maintenance, and repair needs of existing Shack locations.

• Manage the planning and execution of facility upgrades, remodels, and refresh projects.

• Lead, develop, train, and mentor Facilities Managers.

• Monitor Service Channel usage and vendor performance, continuously evaluating and improving

the vendor network.

• Train Operations teams on key maintenance tasks and best practices to support the ongoing

upkeep of their Shacks.

• Ensure preventative maintenance agreements are established and all required maintenance is

completed timely and in accordance with the agreed-upon scope.


Related Experience

• Successful track record in managing facilities in a complex and dynamic environment.

• Experience in developing and implementing strategic facility plans.

• Demonstrated ability to lead and motivate a diverse team.

• Proficient in facility management software and tools.

Created By: Jacob Thiessen November 13, 2026 Version: 3


Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

• Bachelor's degree in Facility Management, Business Administration, or a related field.

• Proven experience in facilities management, with a minimum of 8 years in a leadership role.

• Strong leadership, interpersonal, and communication skills.

• Knowledge of building systems, construction, and facility-related technologies.

• Familiarity with relevant regulations and codes.

Education or Certificate Details

• Bachelor's degree in Facility Management, Business Administration, or a related field.


Education Requirements

• High School Diploma or Equivalent

• Bachelor's Degree


Physical Requirements

• Precise hand/eye coordination

• Basic keyboarding or other repetitive motions

• Operation of heavy equipment or operation of vehicles

• Lifting/pushing objects weighing over 10 lbs.

• Climbing and working in awkward and cramped positions

Benefits at Shake Shack:

A work environment where you can come as you are, share your ideas, have fun, and work collaboratively:

  • Weekly Pay and Performance bonuses

  • Shake Shack Meal Discounts

  • Exclusive corporate discounts for travel, electronics, wellness, leisure activities and more

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance*

  • Employer Paid Life and Disability Insurance*

  • 401k Plan with Company Match*

  • Paid Time Off*

  • Paid Parental Leave*

  • Access to Employee Assistance Program on Day 1

  • Pre-Tax Commuter and Parking Benefits

  • Flexible Spending and Dependent Care Accounts*

  • Development and Growth Opportunities

*Eligibility criteria applies

Pay Range - $107,996.00 - $182,736.00 *The salary paid to a successful applicant will depend on the applicant’s experience, qualifications, business needs and resources, and the candidate’s location.

Click the "Apply" button above to apply for this opening.

About Us

Beginning as a hot dog cart in New York City’s Madison Square Park, Shake Shack was created by Danny Meyer, Founder and CEO of Union Square Hospitality Group and best-selling author of Setting the Table. Shack Fans lined up daily, making the cart a resounding success, and donating all proceeds back to the park beautification efforts. A permanent stand was eventually built…and the rest is Shack history! With our roots in fine dining and giving back to the community, we are committed to high quality food served with a high level of hospitality. Our team members enjoy a positive work environment that is deeply committed to the philosophy that we "Stand for Something Good."

Shake Shack is an Equal Opportunity Employer 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, disability (mental and physical), sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, gender expression, medical condition, genetic information, marital, military and veteran status.

Plan Life Care

Work Arrangement: 100% Remote
Eligible Locations: Illinois & United States
Employment Type: Full-Time
Department: Healthcare Operations / Facilities Management
Reports To: Director of Operations
Pay:$28–$38 per hour

Position Overview

Plan Life Care is seeking an experienced Healthcare Facilities & HVAC Operations Specialist to support the organization's healthcare facilities, home-care operations, and property-related service needs.

This position is designed for an experienced HVAC professional, facilities technician, service manager, dispatcher, estimator, or maintenance specialist who wants to apply their technical knowledge in a remote healthcare operations environment.

The Specialist will coordinate HVAC, building systems, maintenance requests, vendors, preventive maintenance, service documentation, and facilities-related projects from a remote location.

This is not a field technician position. The selected candidate will use their technical knowledge to coordinate and oversee service activities performed by qualified local technicians and contractors.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate HVAC and facilities service requests for healthcare-related locations and operational properties.
  • Review incoming maintenance requests and determine appropriate service requirements.
  • Coordinate local HVAC technicians, contractors, and maintenance vendors.
  • Schedule preventive maintenance, inspections, repairs, and service appointments.
  • Review technician reports, estimates, invoices, and service documentation.
  • Track open work orders from initial request through completion.
  • Monitor recurring HVAC and facilities issues and identify opportunities for corrective action.
  • Assist with evaluating HVAC service estimates and vendor recommendations.
  • Maintain accurate digital maintenance and facilities records.
  • Coordinate emergency or urgent facilities issues with appropriate vendors and management.
  • Communicate with operations leadership regarding maintenance status, outstanding issues, and potential risks.
  • Assist with preventive maintenance planning and facility service schedules.
  • Support documentation related to facility operations, safety, and regulatory requirements.
  • Help identify opportunities to reduce unnecessary service costs and improve operational efficiency.
  • Coordinate multiple vendors and service requests while maintaining accurate records.
  • Provide technical guidance to non-technical members of the operations team when appropriate.

Healthcare Environment

The successful candidate will support facilities and operations within a healthcare and home-care environment.

Experience with healthcare facilities is valuable, but direct healthcare experience is not required if the candidate has strong HVAC, facilities, maintenance, or service-management experience.

The position requires an understanding that healthcare environments may have additional requirements involving:

  • Client and employee safety.
  • Environmental comfort.
  • Preventive maintenance.
  • Service documentation.
  • Vendor coordination.
  • Confidentiality.
  • Facility readiness.
  • Timely response to maintenance concerns.

Ideal Background

We are particularly interested in candidates with backgrounds such as:

  • HVAC Service Technician
  • HVAC Technician
  • HVAC/R Technician
  • HVAC Service Manager
  • HVAC Dispatcher
  • HVAC Estimator
  • Facilities Manager
  • Facilities Maintenance Specialist
  • Building Maintenance Supervisor
  • Maintenance Coordinator
  • Commercial HVAC Professional
  • Property Maintenance Professional
  • Healthcare Facilities Professional

Qualifications

Required

  • 3+ years of HVAC, facilities, maintenance, service coordination, or related technical experience.
  • Strong understanding of HVAC systems and service operations.
  • Ability to review and understand HVAC service reports and recommendations.
  • Strong organizational and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication.
  • Ability to coordinate contractors and vendors professionally.
  • Strong computer and administrative skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple work orders and priorities.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.

Preferred

  • HVAC/R certification or technical training.
  • EPA 608 certification.
  • Healthcare facilities experience.
  • Commercial HVAC experience.
  • Facilities management experience.
  • Service dispatch or coordination experience.
  • Experience with work-order management systems.
  • Experience reviewing HVAC estimates and invoices.
  • Experience with preventive maintenance programs.
  • Previous remote-work experience.

Remote Work Requirements

This is a 100% remote position.

Applicants must:

  • Reside in Florida or another U.S. state.
  • Be legally authorized to work in the United States.
  • Have reliable high-speed internet.
  • Have a dependable computer and professional home workspace.
  • Be available during established business hours.
  • Be comfortable communicating by phone, email, video conference, and online systems.
  • Be capable of working independently and managing priorities without direct in-person supervision.

Compensation

$28–$38 per hour

The final rate will be based on HVAC experience, technical expertise, certifications, facilities experience, healthcare experience, and overall qualifications.

Why Join Plan Life Care?

This is an opportunity for an experienced HVAC or facilities professional to transition into a professional remote healthcare operations role while continuing to use the technical knowledge developed throughout their career.

Instead of performing physically demanding field work every day, you will use your experience to coordinate service providers, evaluate maintenance needs, manage work orders, and help keep healthcare operations running efficiently.

How to Apply

Qualified candidates should submit a current résumé highlighting their HVAC, facilities, maintenance, service-management, or technical operations experience.

Candidates with strong technical experience who are interested in transitioning into a remote healthcare operations position are encouraged to apply.

Plan Life Care
Remote – Florida & United States

The Manager, Facilities Transformation & Capital Programs uses facilities spend, robust asset and work order data, vendor performance, and operational trends to identify root causes, shape strategy, reduce R&M costs, improve asset performance, and guide smarter maintenance capital decisions across the company-owned restaurant portfolio.

Reporting to the Vice President, Facilities Management, the Manager leads execution of facilities-related projects from planning through delivery, including maintenance capital governance, program development, stakeholder communication, and results tracking. This role translates insights into business cases and long-range capital plans, including PCI programs that proactively replace critical equipment, reduce R&M and utility costs, mitigate risk, and support compliance. The Manager ensures capital and resources are focused on the right assets, restaurants, and business needs while keeping partners aligned on priorities, risks, decisions, and outcomes.


RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead enterprise facilities performance analysis across spend, vendors, assets, work orders, capital, and operational trends. Identify root causes, recurring issues, cost drivers, risk areas, and opportunities to improve restaurant performance and reduce downtime. Apply root cause analysis to reduce recurring costs, inform targeted training needs, strengthen vendor accountability, and support manufacturer performance conversations that benefit both company-owned restaurants and franchisees.

  • Translate facilities analysis into executive-ready insights, business cases, prioritization recommendations, and decision-support materials that inform leadership decisions, capital planning, vendor performance, and operational priorities. Own enterprise Facilities insights requests, including ad hoc business inquiries where asset, work order, vendor, or performance data can support better decision-making. Use analysis to advance programs that improve restaurant performance, unlock efficiencies, and reduce costs.
  • Own Facilities projects and programs end to end, from planning through execution, closeout, and results tracking. This includes the Proactive Capital Investment program, cyclical facility programs such as roof replacements, parking lots, and paint, and ad hoc installations or initiatives. Through PCI, this role drives proactive replacement of critical equipment and programs that reduce R&M and utility costs, mitigate downtime and safety risks, and support compliance. Establish project plans, timelines, milestones, risk tracking, stakeholder communication, and regular status reporting. Support maintenance capital governance by using asset data, R&M trends, operational risk, and financial impact to prioritize investment in the highest-need, highest-value assets and restaurants.
  • Develop and maintain the Facilities communication strategy for internal and external stakeholders. Ensure clear, timely messaging on project schedules, program updates, process changes, performance insights, and decisions needed to keep partners aligned.
  • Partner across Facilities, Finance, Operations, Development, Procurement, and vendors to connect insights to action, remove barriers, and ensure initiatives are field-ready, financially sound, and operationally sustainable.

EDUCATION QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum: 4 yr Degree in Facilities Management, Business, Finance, Analytics, Construction Management, Operations, or related field.

Preferred: Project Management Professional (PMP), change management, data analytics, or related certification.

EXPERIENCE QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum: 10+ years of experience in facilities management, project management, business analytics, operations, finance, restaurant operations, retail facilities, or related fields.

  • Experience translating data and performance trends into actionable recommendations for leadership and operational stakeholders.
  • Experience managing cross-functional projects, programs, timelines, risks, and stakeholder communication.
  • Experience developing executive-ready summaries, business cases, performance updates, or decision-support materials.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities while driving measurable outcomes.
  • Strong analytical, communication, organization, and problem-solving capabilities.

Preferred

  • Experience in multi-unit restaurant, retail, hospitality, healthcare, or commercial facilities environments.
  • Experience with CMMS, work order management systems, Power BI, financial reporting tools, project management tools, or facilities analytics platforms.
  • Experience supporting capital planning, vendor performance management, asset lifecycle planning, or proactive maintenance programs.
  • Experience developing communication plans, stakeholder updates, and change management materials for field or operations audiences.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Deep facilities management expertise with the ability to connect asset performance, R&M cost drivers, vendor execution, and restaurant operational impacts into practical business recommendations
  • Ability to leverage reporting and analytics tools to identify trends, quantify opportunities, and drive action
  • Strong business acumen with the ability to connect operational, financial, and field impacts into practical recommendations
  • Strong project and program management skills, including planning, scheduling, risk management, status reporting, and follow-through
  • Ability to translate complex data and technical findings into clear, concise, executive-ready communication
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to tailor messaging for executives, Operations, Finance, vendors, and field leaders
  • Ability to build trusted cross-functional partnerships and influence outcomes without direct authority
  • Strong continuous improvement mindset with the ability to standardize routines, improve processes, and create repeatable communication and reporting practices
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and follow-through
  • Ability to manage confidential information and sensitive business priorities with discretion
